info.title: Curvet API
info.description:
The public API at /api/v1, as the code answers today (generated by backend/scripts/buildOpenApi.js from backend/api/v1/schemas; do not edit by hand).

Two routers share the prefix and answer errors in two shapes: the OpenAI-compatible routes (/chat/completions, /embeddings, /models, /public/models) in OpenAI's envelope (OpenAIErrorResponse), and the /playground routes as {success:false, error:"<sentence>", …} (PlaygroundErrorResponse). On these two routers every error carries a stable `code`, its `type`, `retryable` and the request id (the request id once the router has seen the request): a model or provider failure the shared StepError contract's code and status, anything else an ApiErrorCode. The server's own answers for a path under /api/v1 (a path no router serves, a body that does not parse or is over 5 MB, the per-IP rate limit) come in the same shapes: OpenAI's on the OpenAI-style paths, the native one elsewhere. Not covered yet: the other routers under /api/v1 — voice (/voice), food (/food), custom models (/playground/custom-models), enterprise (/enterprise), the CLI's (/auth/cli, /cli/agency, /cli/enterprise) and developer (/developer) — which answer their own refusals in shapes of their own and are not described here; the server's own answers for their paths (above) are native-shaped.

Changes (November 2026). Added everywhere: `code`, `type`, `retryable` and the request id on every error above; Retry-After and X-Curvet-Limit-* on every 429 of the key's own limits, giving when the call would pass. Answers that changed: on the OpenAI-style routes a 403 is `permission_error` (was `authentication_error`) and an auth or policy 500 `api_error` (was `invalid_request_error`); several OpenAI-style 500 and 503 answers carry `code` `unknown` or `provider_unavailable`, and POST /embeddings' own 400s `model_required` or `invalid_parameter` with the field in `param` (all were null); the server's own answers on the OpenAI-style paths are OpenAI-shaped (the string `error` and the top-level `message` and `retryAfter` are gone there); the per-IP 429's `retryAfter` is the real wait (was always 900); POST /embeddings answers an input over the model's limit, text or token ids, 413 `input_too_long` (was 400); a workflow run that stops answers its failing step's status (402, 502, …), or 404, 403, 409 or 500 (was always 500, with the raw error text); a malformed workflow or run id is 404 (was 500); GET /playground/jobs/{jobId} answers a provider poll failure with the contract's status (was 404 or 500); our own 500s give a fixed sentence (was the raw error text; with NODE_ENV=development the server's own 500 still carries the exception's text in `message`, as before); a media reply's `remainingBalance` is null when the balance cannot be read in time (was a 500); on native paths under /api/v1 (voice, food, enterprise and the CLI's included) the server's own `error` sentence is a specific one ("The request body is not valid JSON.", …) instead of "Something went wrong!" (the old `message` is kept); `rateLimitInfo.resetsAt` and `costCapInfo.resetsAt` are when the call would pass in the rolling window, not a full hour or day from now; an error handed to the server's handler with a `status` below 400 answers 500 under /api/v1 (it answered that status, an error body with a success status), as Express's own error handler does.

Authentication: a secret key (sk_curvet_…) or, while they are still accepted, an app's appKey (app_…), in x-app-key or Authorization: Bearer.

200.description: The curated chat models this key can call.

post.description: OpenAI's Chat Completions, on Curvet's models, strict: the model asked for runs or the call fails, never a substitute. With `stream` the answer is Server-Sent Events.

200.description: The completion; with `stream`, a text/event-stream of OpenAIChatCompletionChunk frames ending in `data: [DONE]`.

schema.description: Server-Sent Events: `data: <JSON>` frames, each an OpenAIChatCompletionChunk (x-curvet-frame-schema), then `data: [DONE]`. `: keepalive` comment lines may arrive between frames.

400.description: A missing model or messages, a field the route refuses (response_format, top_p, stop, seed, the penalties), not a chat model, an image for a model that reads none, an invalid Idempotency-Key, or input the provider refused (bad_input). Also: a body that is not valid JSON (invalid_json).

401.description: No key (missing_api_key), or a key that is unknown (invalid_api_key), revoked (api_key_revoked) or expired (api_key_expired); or an app key (app_…) where only secret keys are accepted (app_key_not_accepted).

403.description: The key's app is not active (app_not_active) or has the API off (api_not_enabled), its developer account is missing or not approved (developer_account_not_found, developer_not_approved), the owner is missing or suspended (user_not_found, account_suspended), or the caller's address is not on the key's IP allowlist (ip_not_allowed). Also: the model is not on the key's list, the key may not use the chat category, or the organization's policy or per-call ceiling refuses the model.

404.description: No such model, or another account's custom model (model_not_found); or a model that is not available (model_unavailable).

post.description: Runs a visual-builder workflow the key's owner owns or edits, and waits for it; with async, answers 202 at once.

parameters.name: async
parameters.description: `true` or `1`: answer 202 with a runId instead of waiting.

schema.description: The same fields as form fields; any file part is read as an upload (at most 10 files, 25 MB each).

200.description: The run executed: `success` is false when steps failed inside a run that carried on past them (see nodeErrors). Check `success`, not only the status.

400.description: An invalid Idempotency-Key, or a step that stopped the run on its input or setup (bad_input, needs_input, setup_error). Also: a body that is not valid JSON (invalid_json).

401.description: No key (missing_api_key), or a key that is unknown (invalid_api_key), revoked (api_key_revoked) or expired (api_key_expired); or an app key (app_…) where only secret keys are accepted (app_key_not_accepted).

402.description: A step could not be paid for (insufficient_credits).

403.description: The key's app is not active (app_not_active) or has the API off (api_not_enabled), its developer account is missing or not approved (developer_account_not_found, developer_not_approved), the owner is missing or suspended (user_not_found, account_suspended), or the caller's address is not on the key's IP allowlist (ip_not_allowed). Also: the key's owner neither owns nor edits the workflow (workflow_access_denied).

404.description: No such workflow, also for an id that is not a valid workflow id or a workflow deleted as the run started (workflow_not_found); or a step's model is not available (model_unavailable).

409.description: The run was stopped before it finished (workflow_run_stopped, with `runId`); or an Idempotency-Key conflict (idempotency_key_in_use, idempotency_key_not_replayable).

410.description: The model was retired by its provider (model_retired).

413.description: A file over 25 MB or more than 10 files (upload_too_large), or a step's input too long for its model (input_too_long). Also: a JSON body over 5 MB (body_too_large).

422.description: The Idempotency-Key was used with a different request, or a step was blocked by its model's content rules (content_policy).

424.description: A connected app a step uses needs attention (connection_needed).

429.description: The key's hourly request limit (rate_limit_exceeded), daily cost cap (daily_cost_cap_exceeded) or a credit budget (budget_exhausted), with Retry-After and X-Curvet-Limit-*; a step's limit or a busy provider (limit_reached, provider_busy); or too many requests from this IP address (ip_rate_limited).

500.description: A failure of Curvet's own stopped the run or kept it from starting (unknown; the sentence is fixed, the cause is in Curvet's request log). `runId` names the run when it was created.

502.description: The provider failed, or answered with nothing usable (provider_down, no_output).

503.description: The model is temporarily unavailable: Curvet's account at the provider, or the provider's circuit is open (provider_unavailable; not retryable, so no Retry-After).

403.description: The key's app is not active (app_not_active) or has the API off (api_not_enabled), its developer account is missing or not approved (developer_account_not_found, developer_not_approved), the owner is missing or suspended (user_not_found, account_suspended), or the caller's address is not on the key's IP allowlist (ip_not_allowed).

appKeyHeader.name: x-app-key
appKeyHeader.description: A secret key (sk_curvet_…) or an appKey (app_…).

bearerAuth.description: The same key as a Bearer token. x-app-key wins when both are sent.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Send the same key again within 24 hours and the first request's answer is replayed instead of running and charging again (middleware/idempotency.js). 1 to 255 visible ASCII characters; a UUID is a good choice. A request that failed (status 400 or above) does not keep its key.

XCurvetRequestId.description: This request's id in Curvet's request log (middleware/apiRequestLog.js), minted for every request that reaches the API routers. Quote it to support; a replayed answer has its own.

XCurvetTraceId.description: The correlation id of the request (middleware/traceContext.js): the caller's own x-curvet-trace-id or x-request-id when it sent a well-formed one, else a new id. On every answer of the server.

RetryAfter.description: Seconds to wait before trying again. Sent with the 429 of the key's hourly limit, daily cost cap or budget (until the call would pass: the rolling hour or day lets go of the call that has to age out first, or the budget's period ends), of the per-IP limit (ip_rate_limited), of a chat call refused while calls in progress hold the rest of the balance (balance_held: retry when they end) and of a busy provider (provider_busy: the provider's own value when it gave one, else 30); with a retryable 503; and with 409 idempotency_key_in_use (2). Not with a workflow step's own limit (limit_reached), which has no reset time to give.

IdempotentReplayed.description: "true" when this is the stored answer to an earlier request with the same Idempotency-Key (nothing ran and nothing was charged again).

XCurvetCreditsCharged.description: Credits the call cost, the amount the wallet moved. Not on a stream: its cost rides on the closing x_curvet chunk.

XCurvetBilling.description: How the call was billed: `metered` (per token) or `flat` (the model's per-call credit). On a stream too, before the amount is known.

XCurvetTokensIn.description: Input tokens billed (prompt tokens, cached input included).

XCurvetIgnoredParams.description: Request fields the model's provider does not take and that were therefore not sent, comma-separated (of response_format, top_p, stop, seed, frequency_penalty, presence_penalty). Absent when every field was sent. Also on errors.

XCurvetContentStored.description: What of this exchange Curvet keeps (30 days, private), by the retention policy and the owner's setting: `none`, `prompt`, `completion` or `prompt,completion`. Always `none` on /embeddings.

XCurvetLimit.description: The binding credit budget; on a refusal, the limit that refused: the hourly request limit (requests), the daily cost cap (USD) or the budget (credits). Only when the key, its organization or the platform has a budget, or one of the key's limits refused the call.

XCurvetLimitRemaining.description: What is left of X-Curvet-Limit (0 on a refusal).

XCurvetLimitScope.description: Whose limit: key, org or platform (the hourly request limit says key; the daily cost cap says platform).

XCurvetLimitPeriod.description: The limit's period: hour (the hourly request limit), day, week or month.

XCurvetLimitReset.description: When the refusing limit resets (ISO 8601): the hourly request limit, the daily cost cap or a budget. Only on such a 429.

ApiErrorCode.title: ApiErrorCode

ChatPenalty.description: frequency_penalty / presence_penalty. null is the same as absent. Forwarded where the provider honours it; otherwise named in X-Curvet-Ignored-Params.

ChatReasoningEffort.description: How much a model that thinks first may think: none, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh or max (case and surrounding spaces ignored). Never refused: each model is sent it only in the form and with the values its provider was seen to accept (OpenAI and DashScope reasoning_effort, Claude output_config.effort, Gemini thinkingConfig), and anything else — a level the model does not take, another value, another type — is left out and named in X-Curvet-Ignored-Params. Thinking is drawn from the same budget as max_tokens: a small max_tokens with a high level can be spent before any text (an empty answer with finish_reason "length").

anyOf.description: Any other value: accepted, not sent, named in X-Curvet-Ignored-Params.

ChatResponseFormat.description: JSON mode (utils/chatRequestParams.js). null is the same as absent; {type:"text"} is the default and is dropped. Forwarded where the model's provider honours it; otherwise named in X-Curvet-Ignored-Params.

json_schema.description: OpenAI's {name, schema, strict}. Only `schema` is checked: an object, or null.

ChatSeed.description: A safe integer. null is the same as absent. Forwarded where the provider honours it; otherwise named in X-Curvet-Ignored-Params.

ChatStop.description: A string, or an array of strings with at most 4 that are not empty. "", [] and null mean none. Forwarded where the provider honours it; otherwise named in X-Curvet-Ignored-Params.

ChatTopP.description: null is the same as absent. Forwarded where the provider honours it; otherwise named in X-Curvet-Ignored-Params.

CurvetPricing.title: CurvetPricing
CurvetPricing.description: A model's per-token rates in credits per million tokens (services/billing/rateCard.js pricingBlock; for an embedding model services/billing/embeddings.js pricingBlock). Published as `x_curvet_pricing` on GET /models and as `pricing` on GET /playground/models. Only models with a verified token rate have one.

billing.description: `metered` when a call is billed on these rates now; `flat_per_request` when the model's flat per-call credit still applies. Always `metered` for an embedding model.

cached_input.description: Only for models with a cache-read rate.

tiers.description: Only for models priced by prompt size.

minimum_per_request.description: Embedding models only: the minimum charge per request, in credits.

OpenAIChatCompletion.title: OpenAIChatCompletion
OpenAIChatCompletion.description: POST /chat/completions without `stream` (routes/api/openai.js completionObject). What it cost is in the X-Curvet-Credits-Charged, X-Curvet-Billing, X-Curvet-Tokens-In and X-Curvet-Tokens-Out headers, not in the body.

model.description: The model that ran: Curvet's id, also when the request named an alias or a retired id.

content.description: null when the model answered with tool calls only. "" when it answered with nothing and that stands as the answer (charged): finish_reason `length` (cut at max_tokens before any text), `stop` on a request that sent stop sequences, or an empty answer the provider billed more than 1 credit for (a long prompt, or hidden reasoning, shown in usage). Any other empty answer is not a 200: it is the 502 no_output error, and is not charged.

tool_calls.description: Present only when the model called a tool.

finish_reason.description: `stop`, `tool_calls` (when the model called a tool) or `length` (cut at the answer limit); a provider's own value otherwise.

OpenAIChatCompletionChunk.title: OpenAIChatCompletionChunk
OpenAIChatCompletionChunk.description: One `data:` frame of POST /chat/completions with `stream`. The stream is, in order: a chunk with delta {role:"assistant"}; content chunks (delta {content}) and tool-call chunks (delta {tool_calls}); a closing chunk with an empty delta and the finish_reason; when stream_options.include_usage was set and the provider reported usage, a chunk with empty choices and `usage`; a chunk with empty choices and `x_curvet` (what the call cost); then the line `data: [DONE]`, which is not JSON. `: keepalive` comment lines can arrive between frames. A failure after the stream opened is one frame {error} (the OpenAIErrorResponse envelope with every field present) followed by `data: [DONE]`.

id.description: The same id on every chunk of one stream.

created.description: Unix seconds; the same on every chunk.

choices.description: One choice, or none on the usage and x_curvet chunks.

tool_calls.description: OpenAI tool-call deltas, keyed by `index`: id, type and function.name on the first fragment of a call, function.arguments split across the rest.

finish_reason.description: null except on the closing chunk: `stop`, `tool_calls`, `length` or the provider's own value.

x_curvet.description: On the last chunk before [DONE]: what the call cost, the same figure the wallet moved.

OpenAIChatCompletionRequest.title: OpenAIChatCompletionRequest
OpenAIChatCompletionRequest.description: POST /chat/completions. Only what the route refuses with a 400 is a constraint here: a body this schema accepts passes every check the route makes before the model is called, except the ones that depend on the model (a model that is unknown, not a chat model, not on the key's list, or that reads no images). Fields described as "not checked" are passed on as sent; a value of the wrong type fails at the provider or falls back to the default. Fields not listed are ignored.

model.description: A model id from GET /models, an OpenRouter-style alias of one (google/gemini-2.5-flash), a retired id (runs on its successor), or the caller's own custom model (ft:…). Ids are matched case-insensitively.

messages.description: OpenAI chat messages. The items are not checked here; each provider reads role, content (a string or content blocks), tool_calls, tool_call_id and name as it can. Image blocks (type image_url, image or input_image) are read for vision models.

temperature.description: Not checked: read with parseFloat, and anything that is not a number becomes 0.7.

max_tokens.description: Not checked: read with parseInt. Wins over max_completion_tokens when both are sent. Without one, a call billed per token gets the provider's own limit, any other call the model's default (1024 for most).

max_completion_tokens.description: OpenAI's newer spelling of max_tokens. Not checked.

stream.description: Any truthy value streams the answer as Server-Sent Events (OpenAIChatCompletionChunk frames).

stream_options.description: Not checked. `include_usage` truthy adds a usage chunk before the closing x_curvet chunk.

tools.description: OpenAI tool definitions, passed to the provider as sent. Not checked.

tool_choice.description: Passed to the provider as sent. Not checked.

parallel_tool_calls.description: Passed to the provider as sent. Not checked.

imageUrl.description: Curvet extension: one image (an https URL or a data: URI) for a vision model, besides any in the messages. Not checked.

images.description: Curvet extension: images for a vision model, besides any in the messages. Read only when it is an array; its items are not checked.

OpenAIEmbeddingsRequest.title: OpenAIEmbeddingsRequest
OpenAIEmbeddingsRequest.description: POST /embeddings (services/embeddingsGateway.js normaliseRequest). Only what the route refuses with a 400 is a constraint here. Checks that depend on the model are not: token-id input is accepted on OpenAI embedding models only, each input must fit the model's input limit (a lower bound on its tokens, and a character bound), `dimensions` must not exceed the model's vector length and is accepted only by models that support it, and the whole request may carry about 300,000 tokens (about 4 characters each). Fields not listed (user, …) are ignored.

model.description: An embedding model id or one of its aliases (openai/text-embedding-3-small); see GET /playground/models, type "embedding". Anything else is a 404.

input.description: Text, or token ids (OpenAI embedding models only). At most 2048 inputs.

encoding_format.description: `base64`: each vector as little-endian float32 bytes in base64. Default float.

dimensions.description: A shorter vector, on models that support it (up to the model's own length).

OpenAIEmbeddingsResponse.title: OpenAIEmbeddingsResponse
OpenAIEmbeddingsResponse.description: POST /embeddings. Always billed per input token, after the call, on the tokens the provider measured (estimated when it reported none). The charge is also in the X-Curvet-Credits-Charged, X-Curvet-Billing (metered) and X-Curvet-Tokens-In headers.

embedding.description: Floats, or a base64 string when encoding_format was base64.

model.description: Curvet's id, also when the request named an alias.

tokens_estimated.description: Only when the provider reported no token count and it was estimated.

code.description: Always set: an ApiErrorCode (see ApiErrorCode, which includes OpenAI's own `model_not_found` and `insufficient_quota`, the idempotency_key_* codes and a custom model's state codes) or a StepError code (see StepError).

param.description: The request field the refusal is about (`model`, `input`, `dimensions`, `encoding_format`), when it is about one; else null.

provider_status.description: Model or provider failures only: the provider's own HTTP status; null when there was none, and for provider_unavailable.

retryable.description: Whether the same request can succeed later unchanged (after Retry-After, when there is one).

request_id.description: The same value as the x-curvet-request-id header; null on a refusal made before the API router saw the request (a body that does not parse).

limit.description: 429 from the key's own limits only: which limit refused, and when it resets (the native routes' rateLimitInfo / costCapInfo / budgetInfo).
Requests per hour, USD per day, or credits.

used.description: Requests, USD (a string with four decimals, as costCapInfo has it) or credits.

period.description: budget only: day, week or month.

OpenAIErrorResponse.title: OpenAIErrorResponse

OpenAIModel.title: OpenAIModel
OpenAIModel.description: One model, OpenAI-shaped, with Curvet's and OpenRouter's rate cards (routes/api/openai.js modelEntry). GET /models/{model} also answers an embedding model (embeddingModelEntry): it then has `dimensions`, `context_length` is its input limit, `architecture.output_modalities` is ["embeddings"], and there is no `pricing` or `max_output_tokens`. A custom model (`ft:` id, owned_by "custom") has neither rate card unless the catalogue prices it, and no `context_length`.

id.description: Curvet's id, also when the request named an alias.

created.description: A fixed timestamp; the registry has no creation date.

owned_by.description: The provider (openai, anthropic, google, …), or custom.

aliases.description: Other ids this model answers to (OpenRouter-style for chat models). Usually empty.

context_length.description: Chat models: the context window, when the registry has one. Embedding models: the most tokens one input may have.

max_output_tokens.description: The provider's maximum answer, where verified.

dimensions.description: Embedding models only: the vector length.

OpenAIModelList.title: OpenAIModelList
OpenAIModelList.description: GET /models and GET /public/models. Chat models only: the curated CLI set (registry getCliModels). GET /models puts the key owner's callable custom models first and keeps only the key's allowedModels when it has a list; GET /public/models is the full curated set, the same for everyone. Embedding models are never listed here (see GET /playground/models).

OpenAIToolCalls.description: OpenAI tool calls as the provider path returned them.

OpenAIUsage.description: Token counts, normalised across providers: prompt_tokens includes cached input (Anthropic reports it separately and it is added back).

prompt_tokens_details.description: Only when some input was read from the provider's cache.

cache_creation_input_tokens.description: Only when input was written to the provider's cache (Anthropic).

completion_tokens_details.description: Only when the provider reported reasoning tokens.

OpenRouterPricing.description: The same rates in OpenRouter's shape: USD per token, as decimal strings, never in exponent notation (rateCard.openRouterPricing).

Playground3dRequest.title: Playground3dRequest
Playground3dRequest.description: POST /playground/3d (JSON only). Only what the route refuses with a 400 is a constraint here; whether `model` is a known 3D model, and the model's prompt limit (400 PROMPT_TOO_LONG with maxPromptLength), are checked per model. Every field other than model and prompt is passed to the job as its input, unchecked (texture, image, …).

model.description: A 3D model id from GET /playground/models. A retired id runs on its successor. Required.

Playground3dResponse.title: Playground3dResponse
Playground3dResponse.description: POST /playground/3d, 200: the job finished within the route's 30 s wait.

modelUrl.description: The job's output URL: the 3D file (null if the job finished without one).

PlaygroundAnalyticsResponse.title: PlaygroundAnalyticsResponse
PlaygroundAnalyticsResponse.description: GET /playground/analytics: this key's app's usage (services/analyticsService.js getAppUsageAnalytics), from its usage transactions. Amounts are in the transactions' unit. The rows are MongoDB aggregation groups: each key's value is in `_id`.

_id.description: Present (null) when there was any usage: the aggregation's group key.

avgLatency.description: Milliseconds; null when no row recorded a latency.

errorBreakdown.description: Failed calls per error code, most frequent first.

appKey.description: The app's legacy appKey, in full.

PlaygroundAudioRequest.title: PlaygroundAudioRequest
PlaygroundAudioRequest.description: POST /playground/audio (JSON only): text to speech or music. Only what the route refuses with a 400 is a constraint here; whether `model` is a known audio model, and the longest text a model that speaks in parts will take, are checked per model (400 "Text too long: …"). Every field other than model and prompt is passed to the job as its input, unchecked.

model.description: An audio model id from GET /playground/models (capability generation or music; transcription models are served elsewhere). A retired id runs on its successor. Required.

prompt.description: The text to speak, or the music prompt. Required and not empty.

voice.description: A voice id the model knows. Not checked; passed to the job, and it decides how some models split long text.

PlaygroundAudioResponse.title: PlaygroundAudioResponse
PlaygroundAudioResponse.description: POST /playground/audio, 200: the job finished within the route's 30 s wait. Long text that the model speaks in parts is never waited on: it answers 202. `usage.parts` is set when the text was spoken in parts, and `cost` and `credits` are then what the job reserved.

audioUrl.description: The job's output URL (null if the job finished without one).

PlaygroundBalanceResponse.title: PlaygroundBalanceResponse
PlaygroundBalanceResponse.description: GET /playground/balance: the key owner's balance (services/creditService.js getBalanceSummary). An owner with no account record reads as all zeros. Organization members get extra breakdown fields, which differ between a shared organization pool and per-member allocations.

walletBalance.description: USD in the wallet (for a shared-pool member: pool plus own wallet).

totalAvailableUSD.description: USD that can be spent now: wallet, points and any enterprise allocation.

totalCredits.description: Credits that can be spent now.

creditLimit.description: Per-member allocation members only; 0 = no cap.

creditLimitRemaining.description: Per-member allocation members only; null when there is no cap.

PlaygroundChatRequest.title: PlaygroundChatRequest
PlaygroundChatRequest.description: POST /playground/chat. Only what the route refuses with a 400 is a constraint here; checks that depend on the model (unknown, not a chat model, not on the key's list, reads no images) are not. Several fields take a camelCase and an OpenAI snake_case spelling; when both are sent the camelCase one is used and the other is not read (a null camelCase value counts as absent). Fields not listed (tools, …) are ignored: this route sends only each message's role and content.

model.description: A chat model id from GET /playground/models, an OpenRouter-style alias, a retired id (runs on its successor), the key owner's custom model (ft:…), or "auto" / "smart" (picks a priced model from the last message). Required; an unknown id is a 400.

messages.description: Chat messages. Each item's role and content are sent; everything else on it is dropped. The items are not checked here. Image content blocks (type image_url, image or input_image) are read for vision models.

temperature.description: Not checked: read with parseFloat; anything that is not a number becomes 0.7.

maxTokens.description: Not checked: read with parseInt. Wins over max_tokens. Without either, a call billed per token gets the provider's own limit, any other call the model's default (1000 for most).

max_tokens.description: OpenAI's spelling of maxTokens. Not checked.

allowFallbacks.description: Only the boolean true lets another model answer when this one fails (the registry's fallback chain, never dearer). Anything else is strict.

response_format.description: Read only when responseFormat is absent or null; then as responseFormat.

top_p.description: Read only when topP is absent or null; then as topP.

frequency_penalty.description: Read only when frequencyPenalty is absent or null; then as frequencyPenalty.

presence_penalty.description: Read only when presencePenalty is absent or null; then as presencePenalty.

reasoning_effort.description: Read only when reasoningEffort is absent or null; then as reasoningEffort. Never refused.

imageUrl.description: One image (an https URL or a data: URI) for a vision model, besides any in the messages. Not checked.

images.description: Images for a vision model, besides any in the messages. Read only when it is an array; its items are not checked.

response.description: The answer's text. Empty only when that stands as the answer (charged): finishReason `length` (cut at maxTokens before any text), `stop` on a request that sent stop sequences, or an empty answer the provider billed more than 1 credit for (a long prompt, or hidden reasoning, shown in usage). Any other empty answer is the 502 no_output error, and is not charged.

finishReason.description: Why the answer stopped, as the gateway reported it (`stop`, `length` when cut at the answer limit, `tool_calls`, or a provider's own value); null when it reported none.

promptTokens.description: Includes cached input. null when the provider reported no usage.

cost.description: USD: the model's flat cost; under metered billing, credits / 100.

credits.description: What was charged: the flat credit, or the settled amount under metered billing.

remainingBalance.description: USD in the owner's own wallet after the charge (wallet only, without points or enterprise credits; not the same figure as the media routes' remainingBalance). Absent when the balance could not be read after a metered charge.

remainingPoints.description: Points (not USD) after the charge. Absent when the balance could not be read after a metered charge.

remainingCredits.description: Credits the owner can still spend after this call: wallet, points and the enterprise or pool credits they may draw on (getBalanceSummary breakdown.totalCredits), the same figure on chat, image and media. null when the balance could not be read within 0.4 s (a slow read never holds up the answer).

model.description: The model asked for, after alias, retired-id and auto resolution. With allowFallbacks the model that answered may differ: see servedModel.

servedModel.description: With allowFallbacks, the model that answered, present only when it is not the one asked for (metadata.model).

requestId.description: The charge's id (the metered job's id under metered billing).

PlaygroundErrorResponse.title: PlaygroundErrorResponse

code.description: Always present: an ApiErrorCode (see ApiErrorCode, which includes the idempotency_key_* codes, upload_too_large, PROMPT_TOO_LONG and a custom model's state codes) or a StepError code (`unknown` for a failure of Curvet's own).

type.description: OpenAI's error type for the code: authentication_error for a bad or missing key, permission_error for a permission or policy refusal, rate_limit_error for a limit (services/apiErrors.js, stepErrors.openAiTypeFor).

retryable.description: Whether the same request can succeed later unchanged (after Retry-After, when there is one).

requestId.description: The x-curvet-request-id header's value. Absent on refusals made before the API router saw the request (a body that does not parse).

jobId.description: A failed media job's id (POST /video, /audio, /3d), or the polled job's (GET /jobs/{jobId}) when polling its provider failed.

runId.description: The workflow run's id (POST /workflows/{id}/run), when the run was created before it stopped.

message.description: PROMPT_TOO_LONG: the longer explanation. On the server's own answers (invalid_json, body_too_large, bad_request, unknown, ip_rate_limited): the text it always carried beside `error`.

retryAfter.description: ip_rate_limited only: seconds until this address may call again (the Retry-After header's value).

required.description: 402 only: the price in USD (the model's cost; on /audio, times the parts it is spoken in).

requiredCredits.description: 402 on /audio only: the price in credits.

available.description: 402 only: the balance in USD (wallet plus points).

rateLimitInfo.description: 429 rate_limit_exceeded, the key's hourly request limit.

costCapInfo.description: 429 daily_cost_cap_exceeded, the key's daily cost cap.

used.description: USD spent, as a string with four decimals ("10.0000").

budgetInfo.description: 429 budget_exhausted, a key, organization or platform credit budget.

PlaygroundImageRequest.title: PlaygroundImageRequest
PlaygroundImageRequest.description: POST /playground/image, as JSON or as multipart/form-data (the same fields as form fields, plus image files). Only what the route refuses with a 400 or 413 is a constraint here; what depends on the model (unknown, not an image model, needs a source image) is not. Files: at most 10, each at most 25 MB (413 upload_too_large). qwen-image-edit reads its source from the first image file; muse-image-1.0 reads every image file. Fields not listed are ignored.

model.description: An image model id from GET /playground/models, or "auto" / "smart" (gpt-image-2 for photo-like prompts, flux-2-klein-4b otherwise). Required; an unknown id is a 400.

prompt.description: Required and not empty. Not otherwise checked.

size.description: Not checked; passed to providers that take a size (OpenAI, Flux, Qwen edit, Muse, Seedream). Default "1024x1024". Gemini models ignore it.

image.description: A source image as an https URL or a data: URI, for ali-* image models (edit) and muse-image-1.0. Read only when it is a non-empty string.

PlaygroundImageResponse.title: PlaygroundImageResponse
PlaygroundImageResponse.description: POST /playground/image. Images are made while the request waits; there is no job.

imageUrl.description: A public URL on Curvet's CDN; the provider's own URL when it answered with one; for Gemini models a data:image/png;base64 URI when storing the image failed; for ali-* models the provider's temporary (about 24 h) URL when re-hosting failed.

remainingBalance.description: USD in the owner's own wallet after the charge (wallet only).

remainingCredits.description: Credits the owner can still spend after this call: wallet, points and the enterprise or pool credits they may draw on (getBalanceSummary breakdown.totalCredits), the same figure on chat, image and media. null when the balance could not be read within 0.4 s (a slow read never holds up the answer).

PlaygroundJobResponse.title: PlaygroundJobResponse
PlaygroundJobResponse.description: GET /playground/jobs/{jobId}: a media job's state (services/jobQueueService.js formatJobResponse). Reading a job that is processing asks the provider at most every 5 s, unless the server runs the media queue (MEDIA_JOBS_QUEUE): then a worker polls the job and a read only reads it. A job of another account is a 404.

metadata.description: The provider's metadata; keys vary by provider.

error.description: Only when failed: the StepError's sentence, exactly as the synchronous route answers the same failure (the provider's own words only for a request, setup or wallet failure). null otherwise.

faultKind.description: Failed jobs only: the classifier's kind (throttled, content_policy, provider_error, …). null for a fault in Curvet's own provider account (stepError.code provider_unavailable), which the synchronous answer does not describe either.

stepError.description: Failed jobs only: the StepError as the synchronous route shows it: providerMessage only for a request, setup or wallet scope, and no faultKind for an account-scope code (derived from faultKind on rows that predate the field).

estimated.description: USD, the list price at creation.

actual.description: USD after completion; null until then.

eta.description: ISO 8601 date-time, when the provider gave one.

PlaygroundMediaJobAccepted.title: PlaygroundMediaJobAccepted
PlaygroundMediaJobAccepted.description: POST /playground/video, /audio and /3d, 202: the job was queued and is still running after the route's 30 s wait (or was never waited on: audio spoken in parts). Poll GET /playground/jobs/{jobId}. The credits are already reserved.

statusUrl.description: A path on this server, not a full URL.

estimatedWaitTime.description: Fixed per route: "1-3 minutes" (video), "10-30 seconds" (audio), "1-2 minutes" (3d).

PlaygroundMediaMetadata.description: The call's own facts. The provider's are in outputMetadata.

model.description: The model that ran (a retired id is replaced by its successor before the call).

PlaygroundMediaOutputMetadata.description: The provider's metadata for the output (duration, resolution, format, …), as the job stored it. Its keys vary by provider. Absent when the job has no output.

PlaygroundMediaUrl.description: The same URL as videoUrl / audioUrl / modelUrl, under one name on /video, /audio and /3d (GET /jobs/{jobId} has it as output.mediaUrl).

parts.description: /audio only, when long text was spoken in parts: how many (each one a provider call, priced as one).

remainingBalance.description: USD the owner can still spend, wallet plus points (getBalanceSummary totalAvailableUSD). Not the same figure as remainingBalance on /chat and /image, which is the wallet alone; remainingCredits is. null when the balance could not be read within 0.4 s: the job is done and charged, and its answer is never failed or held up over the read.

remainingCredits.description: Credits the owner can still spend after this call: wallet, points and the enterprise or pool credits they may draw on (getBalanceSummary breakdown.totalCredits), the same figure on chat, image and media. null when the balance could not be read within 0.4 s (a slow read never holds up the answer).

aliases.description: Other ids POST /playground/chat (chat models) or POST /embeddings (embedding models) accepts for it.

group.description: Only on the key owner's own custom models.

cost.description: Flat price per call in USD. Not always credits / 100: the two are separate columns of the price table.

type.description: chat, image, video, audio, 3d, embedding, or a type no public route serves (design, ui-builder, presentation).

credits.description: Flat price per call in credits (0 for qwen models on an enterprise account). For an embedding model, the per-request minimum.

baseModel.description: Custom models only: the model it was tuned from.

capability.description: `generation`; `transcription` for a speech-to-text audio model (served elsewhere); `music`; `embedding` for an embedding model.

maxOutputTokens.description: The provider's maximum answer, where verified.

pricing.description: Per-token rates; null for a model billed flat per call (image, video, audio, 3d, and chat models without a verified rate).

available.description: Whether a call to it can run now (configured, and not blocked by health).

endpoint.description: The route that serves it, e.g. "POST /api/v1/playground/chat"; null when none does.

surface.description: `api` when an API key can call it.

healthStatus.description: From model vitals; `unknown` when there is no reading.

supportsDimensions.description: Embedding models only: whether `dimensions` is accepted.

maxInputTokens.description: Embedding models only: the most tokens one input may have.

PlaygroundModelsResponse.title: PlaygroundModelsResponse
PlaygroundModelsResponse.description: GET /playground/models: every model type (chat, image, video, audio, 3d, embedding, …), the key owner's own custom models (group "mine") and the embedding models. By default only what this key can call now (available, surface "api"); ?include=all adds the rest, flagged. Filtered by the key's allowedModels and allowedCategories.

rateLimits.description: The key's own hourly request limit and daily cost cap (the platform defaults, 100 requests an hour and $10 a day, when it sets none), and whether they are enforced for this key.

enabled.description: false: neither limit is enforced for this key (the numbers are what would apply).

PlaygroundVideoRequest.title: PlaygroundVideoRequest
PlaygroundVideoRequest.description: POST /playground/video (JSON only). Only what the route refuses with a 400 is a constraint here; whether `model` is a known video model is checked against the registry. Every field other than model and prompt is passed to the job as its input, unchecked: what a model reads (duration, resolution, aspectRatio, image, seed, …) is up to its provider, and a value it refuses fails the job.

model.description: A video model id from GET /playground/models. A retired id runs on its successor. Required.

prompt.description: Required and not empty. Not otherwise checked.

duration.description: Seconds. Not checked; passed to the job.

resolution.description: Not checked; passed to the job.

PlaygroundVideoResponse.title: PlaygroundVideoResponse
PlaygroundVideoResponse.description: POST /playground/video, 200: the job finished within the route's 30 s wait (routes/api/playground.js mediaJobHandler). A job still running answers 202 (PlaygroundMediaJobAccepted); a failed job answers its StepError (PlaygroundErrorResponse with jobId).

videoUrl.description: The job's output URL (null if the job finished without one).

PlaygroundWorkflowDetail.title: PlaygroundWorkflowDetail
PlaygroundWorkflowDetail.description: GET /playground/workflows/{id}: one workflow's summary and the input keys a run reads (services/workflowInputs.js, the runner's own rules).

required.description: Only a Transcribe step with no URL of its own fails a run without its input.

aliases.description: Other keys the run accepts for the same input.

PlaygroundWorkflowList.title: PlaygroundWorkflowList
PlaygroundWorkflowList.description: GET /playground/workflows: the workflows the key owner can run (owner, or an editor added by uid), most recently updated first. Summaries only; GET /playground/workflows/{id} has the inputs.

PlaygroundWorkflowRunAccepted.title: PlaygroundWorkflowRunAccepted
PlaygroundWorkflowRunAccepted.description: POST /playground/workflows/{id}/run with async, 202: the run started. Poll GET /playground/workflows/runs/{runId}.

statusUrl.description: A path on this server, not a full URL.

PlaygroundWorkflowRunRequest.title: PlaygroundWorkflowRunRequest
PlaygroundWorkflowRunRequest.description: POST /playground/workflows/{id}/run, as JSON or as multipart/form-data. Nothing in the body is refused: inputs that are missing or malformed become {} and the run decides what it needs (GET /playground/workflows/{id} lists the input keys). In multipart, each file becomes the input named by its field ({buffer, mimeType, originalname, size}); at most 10 files of 25 MB each (413 upload_too_large).

inputs.description: The run's inputs, keyed by input name. An object, or (useful in multipart) the same object as JSON text; text that is not JSON becomes {}.

includeFullState.description: Anything but false / "false" (any case) keeps `fullState` in a synchronous run's answer. Default: kept.

async.description: true or "true" starts the run and answers 202 with a runId to poll, instead of waiting for it. The query parameter ?async=true or ?async=1 does the same.

PlaygroundWorkflowRunResponse.title: PlaygroundWorkflowRunResponse
PlaygroundWorkflowRunResponse.description: POST /playground/workflows/{id}/run without async: the run that executed (services/workflowRunner.js execute), answered 200 whatever its outcome. A run that finished with failed steps inside it (it carried on past them, or a step lost some of its items) answers 200 with `success: false` and the failures in `nodeErrors`: check `success`, not only the status. A run that stopped answers an error instead (PlaygroundErrorResponse, with `runId`): a failing step's StepError (402 insufficient_credits, 502 provider_down, …), 404 workflow_not_found or 403 workflow_access_denied when the workflow went away or is not the caller's, 409 workflow_run_stopped when someone stopped it, 500 unknown for a failure of Curvet's own.

success.description: false when any step failed (nodeErrors is not empty), even on a 200.

outputs.description: The values of the workflow's output steps, keyed by output name; {output: <last step's value>} when it has none.

fullState.description: Every step's value keyed by step label (or id when it has none). Absent when includeFullState was false.

nodeStateById.description: Every step's value keyed by step id.

nodeErrors.description: Step id → error text, for steps that failed. Empty on a fully successful run.

PlaygroundWorkflowRunStatus.title: PlaygroundWorkflowRunStatus
PlaygroundWorkflowRunStatus.description: GET /playground/workflows/runs/{runId}: a run's progress, and its result once completed. A run of another account is a 403.

currentNode.description: The step running now; null when none is.

waitingOn.description: Only while status is waiting: the Review step the run is parked at.

result.description: Only when completed: the stored result (outputs, fullState, byNodeId, skipped, …). fullState is included whatever includeFullState the run was started with.

error.description: Only when failed: why the run ended.

endTime.description: ISO 8601 date-time; absent until the run ends.

executionTime.description: Milliseconds; absent until the run ends.

PlaygroundWorkflowSummary.description: One workflow. Shared by the list (closed there) and the detail (which adds inputs).

StepError.title: StepError
StepError.description: What went wrong with a model call, in the one shape every surface reads (shared/workflow-core/stepError.mjs makeStepError, filled by backend/services/stepErrors.js). Carried as `stepError` on Playground-router errors and failed jobs. Fields after `message` appear only when known. `providerMessage` and `providerStatus` are never set for an account-scope code (`provider_unavailable`): a provider's 402 or 401 there is Curvet's own account. On the public API (error bodies, a failed job's status) `providerMessage` is shown only for a request, setup or wallet scope, and `faultKind` never for an account-scope code; what a Job stores is unchanged.

code.description: The contract's code. Its HTTP status on the public API: content_policy 422, input_too_long 413, bad_input 400, needs_input 400, no_output 502, model_retired 410, model_unavailable 404, provider_down 502, provider_busy 429, provider_unavailable 503, timeout 504, insufficient_credits 402, limit_reached 429, connection_needed 424, setup_error 400, upstream_failed 424, interrupted 503, unknown 500.

message.description: The sentence to show; at most 600 characters.

providerMessage.description: The provider's own words, when safe to show. Never for an account-scope code.

modelName.description: Its display name, from the registry.

servedModel.description: The model that actually ran, after a fallback.

providerStatus.description: The provider's own HTTP status. Never for an account-scope code.

faultKind.description: The classifier's kind it came from (billing, throttled, provider_error, …), for support.

ref.description: A job or request id the caller can quote.
